source.title: Scaling Trends for Multi-Hop Contextual Reasoning in Mid-Scale Language Models

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Appendix A.2 reports 300 total trials and 150 per scenario type, which conflicts with the main text's 120 total trials and 15 per scenario type per model.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures multi-hop task accuracy across models with different parameter counts and fits scaling curves, but uses synthetic reasoning accuracy rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study tests task accuracy versus model size, not the original claim's loss scaling, extrapolation of held-out loss, or compute-optimal allocation. The 70B reference point is from prior literature, not an experimental result. Results about multi-agent benefits, task structure, entity extraction, hop count, and rule-based methods are not rows unless they directly measure performance across scale; cited findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures synthetic multi-hop task accuracy for four off-the-shelf models of different sizes and fits accuracy-vs-parameter curves. That is a new, small, confounded setting for V6. It does not measure pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is incomplete. The authors' main conclusions are: (1) rule-based methods win on structured tasks and LLM agents on multi-hop tasks; (2) multi-agent gains appear only for capable base models; (3) MoE reasoning tracks active rather than total parameters (suggestive); (4) LLaMA-3 8B beats LLaMA-2 13B. Overall, reasoning depends more on effective use of capacity than on sheer parameter count. The ~50B threshold is offered only as a speculative hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures synthetic multi-hop task success across four mid-scale models and fits accuracy curves; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or perform a controlled training-compute scaling sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance varies by model and single-agent versus multi-agent configuration. The authors also note prompt sensitivity but do not exhaustively optimize prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Multi-agent coordination improves contextual success for stronger base models (+46.7pp for LLaMA-3 8B) but not for weaker ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from agent scaffolding depend on base-model capability.

record.problems: Only four model configurations are tested, and model families differ in training data and methodology, confounding parameter-count comparisons. The authors note 15 trials per condition in the main text, relatively large standard errors, synthetic tasks, and prompt sensitivity. The reported trial totals also conflict with Appendix A.2. The supplementary threshold fit uses a literature-reported 70B point and is explicitly described as speculative.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The study's structured-task and rule-based results, entity-extraction scores, multi-agent ablations, and hop-complexity findings do not report the scale relationship named by V6.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No extrapolation of loss from small runs.
No controlled shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime.
No prediction from pretraining loss. No controlled size sweep within one model family or training recipe. Only 8B–16B models with 15 trials each.
No study of how pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on setup.

missing.what: Structured-task success rates per model and configuration. These are scale-vs-performance data exactly like the contextual rows (e.g., 86.7/86.7/33.3/60.0 single-agent).

Structured-task BIC comparison (power law 12.4 vs sigmoid 14.8) and the fitted power-law parameters. Note a=42.3 and α=0.31 imply accuracy falling with N toward b=95.2, which is implausible for the data.

record.verdict_notes: Trial counts conflict: the main text reports 120 trials (15 per type per model), while Appendix A.2 reports 300/150, 5 seeds and 5 rounds versus 3. All models were run 4-bit quantized via Ollama. The fitted-parameter appendix contains internal inconsistencies: the N0 log-to-parameter conversion and the sign of the power-law fit. Evidence for V6 is weak and confounded; treat the label as low-weight.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured as parameters, tokens, or compute vary.
The study does not fit small-run pretraining losses and compare predictions with much larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
Architecture is not varied at a fixed parameter count under controlled conditions.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling experiment is reported.
The study tests synthetic multi-hop reasoning accuracy across a small set of models, not a broad range of downstream tasks or performance predicted from pretraining loss.
The study compares curve fits for task accuracy, not setup dependence of pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: Contextual task accuracy scaling fit
rows.size_stated: Experimental models include 8B, ∼12B, and 13B active parameters; supplementary fit also includes a 70B literature reference point
rows.operation_detail: Compared power-law and sigmoid fits to contextual task accuracy
rows.note: The 70B reference point is from prior literature and is not experimental data.
rows.check: The BIC comparison uses about four points, one of them a literature-reported 70B value that is not experimental data. A difference of ΔBIC 3.5 between accuracy fits cannot show whether accuracy scales predictably.

rows.subject: Contextual task accuracy scaling fit
rows.size_stated: 8B–13B active parameters in the experimental range; supplementary fit includes a 70B literature reference point
rows.operation_detail: Estimated a sigmoid threshold for contextual task accuracy

conditions.value: Supplementary sigmoid fit with literature reference point

rows.value: ∼50B active parameters; appendix reports N0 = 24.2 ± 0.8 (log scale), corresponding to [42B, 58B] in parameter count
rows.uncertainty: Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (1000 resamples) for N0: [23.1, 25.4] in log scale
rows.note: The authors call the estimate highly speculative and say validation would require experiments with 30B–70B dense models.
rows.check: The extrapolated threshold depends on a cited literature point and is labelled 'highly speculative', so it is not the study's own result. Its stated conversion is also inconsistent: e^24.2 ≈ 32B, and the CI [23.1, 25.4] maps to about 11B–107B, not 42B–58B.

relationships.condition: Four models from different families and generations (8B–16B total parameters), synthetic multi-hop task, single- and multi-agent prompting
relationships.reason: Success does not follow parameter count: LLaMA-3 8B beats LLaMA-2 13B and the 47B-total Mixtral (r1–r8). Ordering depends on whether total or active parameters are counted. Results are confounded by training family.
relationships.display_finding: LLaMA-3 8B outperformed LLaMA-2 13B and Mixtral with 47B total parameters, with size ordering depending on total versus active parameters and comparisons confounded by training family.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
